Subject: Onboarding kickoff — model slate and peak traffic plan

Hi Erica / BrightEdge team —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood. Wanted to kick off the implementation planning discussion so CS/Eng are aligned on the model shortlist and workload sizing we should be sizing for the pilot window. High-level asks below so we can lock the initial runbook this week: 

- Quick confirmation of context window needs (max history per request in tokens).
- Expected daily active users and per-user request frequency for pilot (first 90 days).
- Rough token mix: average prompt tokens vs expected generated tokens.
- Any strict latency SLOs (p95) for critical flows.

From Redwood side we'll propose a 3-model slate (small / medium / large) to balance quality vs unit cost and give guidance on batching/cache settings. Attached is a working workbook with the input table — please populate the left column if you have any traffic estimates handy.

Attachment: brightedge_onboard_workload_estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Next steps: if we can get the estimates by EOD Friday I'll have Grace produce a short model-slate recommendation and cost delta table for Monday's sync.

Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Onboarding kickoff — model slate and peak traffic plan

Thanks Sean — quick answers below from our side after a short ops sync today.

- Context window: most flows need ~1,600 tokens of conversation history (search + user messages). A small subset of analytics summarization may go up to 4,000 tokens but that's <5% of volume.
- Pilot traffic (90 days): we expect ~1,200 DAU, average 3 requests/user/day. Peak concurrency estimate: ~50 concurrent requests at midday.
- Token mix: avg prompt 800 tokens, avg generation 220 tokens. For the 5% long-run summaries, prompts ~3,200 and generation ~800.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile under 700ms for interactive chat flows; summaries can accept up to 2.5s.

We're uploading a CSV with sample session traces to the drive folder (see link). Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk the numbers together.

— Erica
Erica Lim
Head of Product, BrightEdge Analytics

Thanks for the details, Erica — very helpful. Based on the token/profile you sent, preliminary recommendations: 

- Small (cost-optimized): 8-bit quantized LLaMA-2-13B variant, best for short chat and low-latency p95 under 500ms with conservative batching. Use for ~60% of requests.
- Medium (balance): fp16 Mistral-style 30B (inference-optimized kernel) for higher-quality conversational responses and mid-length summaries — target for ~35% of requests.
- Large (heavy summaries): non-quantized 70B-style model with 4k+ context support for the 5% long summaries — keep autoscale pool small and route only those requests; fall back to medium on contention.

Routing/operational notes: 
- Prefix/KV cache for recurring user context can cut token cost by ~18% on the chat flows.
- For the 4k context summaries we recommend an async route with a slightly higher concurrency cap and a longer timeout window to avoid blocking interactive requests.
- We'll set up a canary that routes 10% of traffic to the medium model for the first 2 weeks to validate quality regressions.

Open questions for BrightEdge: 
1) Do you have a strict requirement on model parity vs your current prod provider (e.g., must match certain F1/ROUGE thresholds)?
2) Any PKI/KMS notes for keys we should account for in Private deployment?

I've dropped a short markdown with rationale into the Drive folder (model_shortlist_notes.md). I'll produce the cost delta table after we confirm DAU/requests numbers and any compliance gating.

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
